speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) in the past five years, whether MAS has received complaints against online "finfluencers" who discuss financial content; (b) if so, how many; and (c) whether the Ministry will review the Financial Advisers Act 2001 to regulate the "finfluencer" sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Even if he or she is not remunerated, he will be considered to have provided financial advice if he makes such recommendations or expressions regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Posting of general educational content is not financial advice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Most of these complaints relate to remarks made by finfluencers who were not providing any financial advice and hence, were not subject to regulation by MAS.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think we can all agree that finfluencers do hold significant sway over their viewers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This is often despite finfluencers stating that their words should not be construed as financial advice.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As an unregulated sector, consumers are at risk of hefty losses.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I think in the United States, this was the case when finfluencers were promoting the FTX platform, which subsequently collapsed.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: So, in such a situation, the consumers' only recourse would be pursuing a civil claim against the finfluencer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: To my understanding, there has been no such precedence in our local courts.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Given this, I would like to ask if MAS do have a position on whether finfluencers have a duty of care to their viewers when promoting financial products online and then, in the same breath saying, "Please do not construe my words as financial advice".

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Could MAS work towards a set of industry guidelines to provide both the finfluencers as well as consumers on their respective roles and responsibilities and the due diligence that each party should conduct?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: By doing so, I believe that we can continue to leverage on these influencers to grow our financial literacy among consumers and especially while safeguarding vulnerable consumers.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I want to assure the Member also that consumers who suspect any wrongdoing should lodge a complaint with MAS or the relevant financial advisory firms.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will review reports of breaches or misconduct and take the appropriate regulatory action against the relevant parties found to have breached MAS's regulations, including providing financial advisory services without the appropriate licences or disseminating non-compliant advertisements.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Orders of the Day and Notice of Motion.

speaker: Mr Speaker
